nodes.label: DESI DR2 BAO consistency with DR1, SDSS and supernova distances
nodes.summary: The retained DESI DR2 source reports that its BAO results are consistent with DESI DR1 and SDSS, and that their distance-redshift relationship matches recent supernova compilations over the same redshift range.

assertions.statement: The retained DESI DR2 source reports that its BAO results are consistent with DESI DR1 and SDSS, and that their distance-redshift relationship matches recent supernova compilations over the same redshift range.

scope.population: DESI DR2 BAO results and their reported comparisons with DESI DR1, SDSS, and recent supernova compilations over the same redshift range.
scope.time: The reported DESI DR2 BAO measurements are based on three years of operation. Atlas chronological placement remains unresolved under era=undated.
scope.assumptions: Consistency and matching are attributed only to the DESI Collaboration's stated comparisons in the retained source; the supernova comparison is limited to the same redshift range.
scope.uncertainty: This source-attributed comparison does not assert agreement among all cosmological datasets, establish a unique cosmological model, resolve the nature of dark energy, or claim current-frontier standing.
scope.quantifiers: Restricted to the reported DESI DR2 comparisons with DESI DR1 and SDSS and to the stated supernova distance-redshift relationship over the same redshift range.

support.quote: We present baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements from more than 14 million galaxies and quasars drawn from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 2 (DR2), based on three years of operation.
The DR2 BAO results are consistent with DESI DR1 and SDSS, and their distance-redshift relationship matches those from recent compilations of supernovae (SNe) over the same redshift range.
